claim: RBI consolidated the Sept 2022 Digital Lending Guidelines and the June 2023 DLG guidelines into the RBI (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025
population: All commercial banks, co-op banks, NBFCs incl. HFCs doing digital lending
source_title: Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025 (RBI/2025-26/36, DOR.STR.REC.19/21.07.001/2025-26)
notes: Annex III repeals: 24-Jun-2020 FPC/outsourcing circular; 02-Sep-2022 Guidelines on Digital Lending; 08-Jun-2023 DLG guidelines. In force immediately except para 6 (multi-lender, from 1-Nov-2025) and para 17 (DLA reporting to CIMS, from 15-Jun-2025).

claim: For NBFCs, digital lending/DLG instructions were re-housed on 28-Nov-2025 in the RBI (Non-Banking Financial Companies - Credit Facilities) Directions, 2025 (DLG in a chapter on loss sharing)
source_title: Vinod Kothari Consultants, 'The Great Consolidation'; nbfccompliance.com note on NBFC Credit Facilities Directions 2025
notes: Secondary sources only (law-firm/consultant); I could not open the RBI text of the consolidated NBFC direction. Substance of DL/DLG rules reported as carried over unchanged. Vinod Kothari notes NBFC version drops references to revolving lines of credit.

claim: DLG cover on a loan portfolio is capped at 5% of the amount disbursed out of that portfolio; for implicit guarantees the provider may not bear performance risk beyond the equivalent of 5%
population: DLG arrangements between an RE and an LSP/other RE in digital lending
source_title: RBI (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025, para 23 (was para 6 of the 08-Jun-2023 DLG guidelines)
notes: 2025 wording: 'shall not exceed five per cent of the total amount disbursed out of that loan portfolio at any given time'. The DLG set is a fixed, identifiable portfolio - not dynamic (para 23(ii)). No 2026 change to the cap found.

claim: Only an LSP (or another RE acting as LSP) with an outsourcing arrangement may provide DLG, and the LSP must be a company incorporated under the Companies Act 2013
source_title: RBI (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025, para 18; DLG guidelines 08-Jun-2023 para 3
notes: An LLP or partnership cannot give DLG. RE needs a board-approved DLG policy; provider must give an auditor-certified declaration of aggregate DLG outstanding and past default rates (para 19).

claim: DLG may be accepted only as (a) cash deposited with the RE, (b) FD with a scheduled commercial bank with lien marked to the RE, or (c) bank guarantee in favour of the RE
source_title: RBI (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025, para 22; DLG guidelines 08-Jun-2023 para 5
notes: Must be funded upfront - the LSP locks up 5% of disbursals as cash/FD/BG. A BG costs the LSP a bank commission and usually needs cash margin (not priced here).

claim: RE must invoke DLG within 120 days overdue; DLG tenor must be at least the longest loan tenor in the portfolio
source_title: RBI (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025, para 26; DLG guidelines 08-Jun-2023 paras 9-10
notes: NPA recognition and provisioning stay with the RE regardless of DLG (para 24); invoked DLG is not set off against individual loans.

claim: No DLG is allowed on revolving credit facilities offered digitally or on credit cards
source_title: RBI (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025, para 20
notes: Relevant to the FD-secured card line: the app cannot give first-loss cover on card or credit-line books. Also barred: DLG on loans already under CGTMSE-type trust guarantees, and on NBFC-P2P loans.

claim: A Bueno-style arrangement (LSP pays lender a fixed 18% IRR and bears 100% of default losses) is NOT permitted today: any contract 'called by whatever name' or implicit guarantee linked to portfolio performance is a DLG and is capped at 5%
unit: cap on risk borne by LSP
source_title: DLG guidelines 08-Jun-2023 Annex para 2.1 (definition) and para 6 (cap); carried into RBI (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025 paras 4 and 23
notes: Definition: 'A contractual arrangement, called by whatever name... Any other implicit guarantee of similar nature linked to the performance of the loan portfolio of the RE and specified upfront, shall also be covered under the definition of DLG.' Cap para: 'In case of implicit guarantee arrangements, the DLG Provider shall not bear performance risk of more than the equivalent amount of five per cent of the underlying loan portfolio.' A fixed-return promise to the lender is itself performance-risk transfer.

claim: Only DLG conforming to the rules escapes treatment as 'synthetic securitisation' (and 'loan participation'); synthetic securitisation is not permitted under the 2021 Securitisation Directions, so a structure beyond the 5% cap is caught
value: para 29(ii) DL Directions 2025; para 2 of 08-Jun-2023 circular
source_title: RBI (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025 para 29(ii); DLG circular RBI/2023-24/41 para 2; Securitisation of Standard Assets Directions 2021 para 6(c)
notes: Para 29(ii): 'DLG arrangements ... conforming to the instructions laid down in Chapter VI ... shall not be treated as synthetic securitisation as defined under para 6(c) of Master Direction - RBI (Securitisation of Standard Assets) Directions, 2021 ... and shall also not attract the provisions of loan participation'. The inference that the securitisation MD prohibits synthetic securitisation is from secondary sources (Vinod Kothari, CBFL NLU Delhi); I did not open the MD text itself.

claim: Feb 2026: RBI let NBFCs take DLG into account when computing ECL provisions (IRACP Amendment Directions 2026); DLG must be integral to the loan contract and ECL recomputed after each invocation
source_title: Business Standard, 'RBI allows NBFCs to factor DLG in determining provisions under ECL'; KNM India note on IRACP Amendment Directions 2026
notes: Date inferred from the Business Standard URL (page returned 403). Provisioning relief only - no change to the 5% cap was reported. Makes 5% DLG slightly more valuable to NBFC partners.

claim: Any fees/charges payable to an LSP must be paid directly by the lender (RE); the LSP may not charge or collect them from the borrower
source_title: RBI (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025, para 9(iv)
notes: 'RE shall ensure that any fees, charges, reimbursements, etc. payable to LSP are paid directly by the RE and are not charged to or collected from the borrowers separately by LSP.' So app revenue from loans = sourcing/servicing fee from the lender (plus DLG-linked economics), never a borrower fee. Repayments must go straight to the RE's account - no pass-through or LSP-controlled fund flow (para 9).

claim: Every retail and MSME term loan sanctioned on/after 1-Oct-2024 needs a Key Facts Statement with an all-in APR computation; third-party charges recovered on actual basis (e.g., insurance, legal) are part of APR; charges not in the KFS cannot be levied without explicit consent
population: All REs, new retail & MSME term loans
source_title: RBI circular 'Key Facts Statement (KFS) for Loans & Advances' RBI/2024-25/18 DOR.STR.REC.13/13.03.00/2024-25
notes: DL Directions 2025 para 8(i) requires the KFS for digital loans and para 4(i) adopts this APR definition. Because the LSP fee is paid by the RE and recovered through pricing, it is inside the APR the borrower sees.

claim: Digital borrowers get a cooling-off period (board-set, minimum 1 day) to exit by paying principal plus proportionate APR with no penalty
source_title: RBI (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025, para 10(i)
notes: Any LSP fee the lender pays on a loan that is cancelled in cooling-off is at risk - model a clawback.

claim: From 1-Nov-2025 an LSP tied to several lenders must show a digital view of ALL matching offers (lender name, amount, tenor, APR, monthly repayment, penal charges, link to each KFS), name the unmatched lenders, use a consistent documented matching method, and not push any lender (no dark patterns); ranking allowed only on a publicly pre-disclosed metric
source_title: RBI (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025, para 6
notes: Limits the ability to steer workers to the lender paying the highest LSP fee.

claim: LSPs may not store borrower personal data beyond basic minimal data (name, address, contact details) needed for their contracted role; all data on servers in India (if processed abroad, deleted and brought back within 24 hours); DLAs must not access files/media, contacts, call logs, telephony
value: basic minimal data only; India servers; 24h
source_title: RBI (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025, paras 12(i), 13(i), 13(iv)
notes: Tension with the savings-first thesis: savings history captured as a savings/MF distributor is a different data role, but using it for underwriting on behalf of a lender needs explicit need-based consent with audit trail. No biometric data may be stored by the RE/LSP unless allowed by law.

claim: The RE and any LSP with a borrower interface must each appoint a nodal grievance redressal officer, displayed on website and app; RE must list its LSPs and their DLAs on its website and report DLAs to RBI (CIMS) from 15-Jun-2025
source_title: RBI (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025, paras 5, 11, 17
notes: RBI publishes the reported DLA list, so an unlisted app is visibly unauthorised.

claim: Minimum Net Owned Fund for NBFC-ICC rises to Rs 10 crore; glide path for existing NBFC-ICCs: Rs 2 cr (2021) -> Rs 5 cr by 31-Mar-2025 -> Rs 10 cr by 31-Mar-2027
population: NBFC-ICC (also NBFC-MFI and NBFC-Factors reach Rs 10 cr by 31-Mar-2027)
source_title: RBI circular 'Scale Based Regulation (SBR): A Revised Regulatory Framework for NBFCs' RBI/2021-22/112
notes: Glide path: NBFC-ICC 2 -> 5 (Mar-2025) -> 10 (Mar-2027); NBFC-MFI 5 (2 in NE) -> 7 (5 in NE) -> 10; NBFC-Factors 5 -> 7 -> 10. Vinod Kothari reports the Nov-2025 consolidated directions set NBFC-MFI at Rs 5 cr rather than 7 (unverified). A new applicant is generally advised to bring Rs 10 cr (advisory sites), i.e. this is equity the founder must raise before lending on own book.

claim: RBI's Citizen's Charter timeline for an application for grant of NBFC Certificate of Registration (via PRAVAAH) is 90 days from a complete application
source_title: RBI Citizen's Charter (row 'Application for grant of CoR as NBFC')
notes: Practitioners quote 90-180 days at RBI and 8-14 months end-to-end incl. incorporation and capital infusion (incorpx.io, treelife.in - advisory firms, lower reliability). Use 6-12 months base, 18+ months high.

claim: RBI is still granting new NBFC CoRs, but the number of registrations (and cancellations) declined in 2023-24; RBI cancelled 143 CoRs that year
source_title: RBI Report on Trend and Progress of Banking in India 2023-24, ch. VI para VI.8 and Chart VI.3
notes: The count of NEW CoRs granted is only in Chart VI.3 (not extractable as text); I could not find a published 2024-25 or 2025-26 count. Treat 'RBI is granting new licences' as true but slow and selective.

claim: From 1-Apr-2026 NBFCs with no public funds AND no customer interface and assets < Rs 1,000 cr ('Unregistered Type I NBFC') are exempt from registration; a customer-facing lender (Type II) must still register
source_title: Legal 500 / Ahlawat & Associates, 'RBI Amendments 2026: A New Category for NBFC Registration and Exemptions'; Khaitan & Co ERGO 5-May-2026
notes: Law-firm summary; RBI text not opened. Irrelevant to a worker-facing lender (it has a customer interface), so an own-NBFC route still needs full registration and Rs 10 cr NOF. One-time window to surrender CoR open till 30-Sep-2026.

claim: RBI (Lending Against Gold and Silver Collateral) Directions, 2025 issued 6-Jun-2025 (updated 29-Sep-2025); lenders must comply no later than 1-Apr-2026
population: Commercial banks, co-op banks, all NBFCs
source_title: RBI (Lending Against Gold and Silver Collateral) Directions, 2025 - RBI/2025-26/47 DOR.CRE.REC.26/21.01.023/2025-26, para 4
notes: Para 4: 'shall be complied with as expeditiously as possible but no later than April 1, 2026.' Loans sanctioned earlier stay under the old rules. LTV for consumption loans: <=Rs 2.5 lakh 85%; Rs 2.5-5 lakh 80%; >Rs 5 lakh 75% (para 19). Coin collateral capped at 50 g gold / 500 g silver.

claim: Lenders may not lend against primary gold/silver or against financial assets backed by primary gold/silver (e.g., gold ETF units, gold mutual fund units), nor finance purchase of gold in any form
source_title: RBI (Lending Against Gold and Silver Collateral) Directions, 2025, para 12; definition para 6(x)
notes: 'Primary gold/silver' = 'Gold and silver in any form other than in the form of a jewellery, ornaments and coins'. The Direction does not mention 'digital gold' by name.

claim: Digital gold counts as primary gold, so loans against digital gold are barred
source_title: Upstox news, 'No gold loan against gold mutual funds and ETFs, only ornaments, jewellery, and coins allowed: RBI'
notes: Confirmed as the consistent reading: digital gold is vaulted bullion (not jewellery/ornament/coin), so it falls within 'any form other than jewellery, ornaments and coins'. The RBI text does not name digital gold, so this rests on the definition plus media/advisory reading, not an explicit RBI statement.

claim: SEBI cautioned the public (Press Release 70/2025) that 'digital gold'/'e-gold' sold by online platforms is neither a notified security nor a regulated commodity derivative, so SEBI investor-protection mechanisms do not apply
source_title: SEBI, 'Caution to public regarding dealing in Digital Gold', Press Release No. 70/2025
notes: SEBI pointed investors to regulated alternatives: gold ETFs, Electronic Gold Receipts, exchange-traded commodity derivatives. Body text summarised from NSDL participant circular / taxguru reproductions.

claim: SEBI chair Tuhin Kanta Pandey said SEBI is not looking to regulate digital gold/e-gold because it is outside SEBI's purview, and no new framework is under consideration
source_title: Business Standard, 'Sebi chief Tuhin Kanta Pandey says not looking to regulate digital gold'; ANI
notes: Said on the sidelines of the National Conclave on REITs and InvITs 2025.

claim: As of Sep-2026 the Finance Ministry is consulting (regulators, banks) on a framework: options include notifying digital gold as a 'security' under SCRA 1956, joint RBI-SEBI oversight, and mandatory 1:1 bullion backing. Nothing final.
source_title: Outlook Money, 'How Safe Is Digital Gold? The Rules Investors May Soon Need'
notes: No government notification found; reports cite unnamed sources (Outlook does not attribute). Same article: market ~USD 3 bn (ET industry estimate); purchases averaged ~Rs 2,500 crore/month Jun-Aug 2026 (World Gold Council, per Outlook); average ticket ~Rs 100. Supports the 'no digital gold at launch' choice.

claim: Industry formed a self-regulatory body, the Digital Precious Metals Assurance Council of India (DPMACI), in May 2026; members MMTC-PAMP, SafeGold, Augmont, PhonePe, BharatPe, MobiKwik, Gullak, LenDenClub, CRED; chair Nirupama Soundararajan
source_title: Entrackr, 'Digital gold and silver players form self regulatory body DPMACI'
notes: Name confirmed as DPMACI. CORRECTION: the brief says it was formed by 'Jar, Gullak etc.' - Jar is NOT in the reported founding-member list (Gullak is). Standards: 1:1 audited physical backing, independent custodian/trustee, ombudsman. It is a voluntary industry body, not a statutory SRO.

claim: Bank loans against securities to individuals: cap Rs 1 crore per individual; LTV ceilings 85% for debt MF units, 75% for other MF units/ETFs/REIT-InvIT units, 60% for listed shares; gold/silver/commodity ETFs are not eligible; effective 1-Jul-2026
unit: % max LTV on debt MF units (banks)
source_title: RBI (Commercial Banks - Credit Facilities) Amendment Directions, 2026 (Revised), dated 30-Mar-2026 (reproduced on taxguru.in)
notes: Draft (Oct-2025) had proposed 75% for debt MFs; the final revised text reads 85%. Liquid funds are a SEBI debt-scheme category, so liquid-fund units should qualify at 85% (inference - the text does not name liquid funds). NBFC LAMF LTVs are set by NBFC policy and were not verified. At Rs 10-100/day savings a LAMF is tiny; lenders typically have minimum loan sizes (not verified).

claim: A bank may not grant advances against term deposits held with other banks - so an FD-backed loan, overdraft or secured card must come from the bank holding the FD
source_title: Master Direction - RBI (Interest Rate on Deposits) Directions, 2025 (01-Apr-2025), para 29.7 (as summarised by IBC Laws)
notes: Same MD: minimum FD tenor 7 days (para 8.1.1); premature withdrawal must be allowed for individual FDs up to Rs 1 crore (para 8.1.3). The FD rail and the FD-secured card must sit at the SAME partner bank. Typical OD-against-FD limits (~90% of FD) are bank policy, not RBI - not verified.

claim: SEBI consultation paper (Jan-2025) proposed a Rs 250 'sachetised' SIP: max 3 per investor across AMCs; Rs 500 incentive to distributor per new investor after 24 instalments, funded from investor-education budgets; NACH/UPI Autopay only; not for debt, sectoral/thematic, mid/small-cap; monthly or fortnightly
source_title: Cafemutual, 'MFDs to get an incentive of Rs 500 for bringing in Rs 250 SIP from new investors: SEBI'; Business Standard 22-Jan-2025
notes: CORRECTION to brief: the proposal funded the incentive from the AMC/AMFI investor-education (IAP/IEAF) budgets - NOT the Investor Education and Protection Fund (IEPF is an MCA fund). Comments closed 6-Feb-2025. PAN-exempt investing via Aadhaar for < Rs 50,000/yr per fund was proposed.

claim: There was NO final SEBI circular; 'Chhoti/Choti SIP' was introduced by AMCs under SEBI letter SEBI/HO/IMD/PoD-1/OW/P/2025/5586/1 dated 20-Feb-2025
source_title: Invesco Mutual Fund notice-cum-addendum 'Introduction of Choti SIP facility' (w.e.f. 1-Aug-2025)
notes: CORRECTION: brief asks for 'the FINAL circular'. The instrument is a SEBI letter to AMFI/AMCs, implemented via AMC addenda (Invesco from 1-Aug-2025; Kotak MF announced Mar-2025). I found no circular number in SEBI's circular list for it.

claim: Choti SIP terms as implemented: exactly Rs 250; only for investors new to the MF industry; max 3 (one each at up to 3 AMCs); any other SIP or lumpsum disqualifies later Choti SIPs; growth option only; MONTHLY frequency only (dates 1-28); minimum commitment 60 instalments (exit allowed, exit load applies); payment only via NACH or UPI Autopay; no top-up/pause/modify
source_title: Invesco Mutual Fund notice-cum-addendum dated 31-Jul-2025, paras 1-8
notes: DAILY frequency is NOT allowed under Choti SIP. Debt funds (so liquid funds) excluded per Cafemutual summary; Invesco's eligible list is equity/hybrid plus a gold ETF FoF. A savings app parking daily saves in a liquid fund cannot use Choti SIP for that leg.

claim: Distributor incentive of up to Rs 500 per Choti SIP investor, paid only after 24 months; forfeited if the SIP stops within 24 months, bounces, or the investor opens another SIP/lumpsum; MFDs may not charge transaction fees
unit: Rs per first-time investor (max, after 24 months)
source_title: Cafemutual, 'Some more clarity on Choti SIP incentives for MFDs'
notes: Trade-press source; funding source of the final incentive not stated. Model it as a lagged, conditional Rs 500 with a high forfeiture rate (see REG-035 on exits).

claim: SBI MF launched 'JanNivesh' Rs 250 SIP on 17-Feb-2025 in SBI Balanced Advantage Fund, with daily, weekly or monthly frequency, via YONO and fintechs (Paytm, Groww, Zerodha); SBI waived transaction fees
source_title: Business Standard, 'Start investing with just Rs 250: SBI's JanNivesh SIP makes MFs accessible'; BusinessToday 17-Feb-2025
notes: Launched in presence of then SEBI chair Madhabi Puri Buch. JanNivesh is an AMC product (daily allowed) distinct from the industry Choti SIP (monthly only).

claim: Choti SIP count reached ~3.22 lakh by June 2026 but with high discontinuation (~26,000 exits in May 2026)
source_title: Business Standard, 'Chhoti SIPs gain scale but face high exit rush amid West Asia conflict' (15-Jul-2026); BS video '26000 exit in May 2026'
notes: Article paywalled/403; figures from search snippets only. Snippet's comparison base ('197,000 in April 2025') is ambiguous and may be April 2026. Rollout was hit by technical glitches per AMFI (BS, 11-Nov-2025).

claim: AMFI ARN registration fee (from 1-Oct-2024): Individual Rs 3,000 (renewal Rs 1,500); Private Ltd company Rs 40,000 (renewal Rs 20,000); Public Ltd Rs 4,00,000; NBFC Rs 1,00,000; EUIN per employee Rs 1,500 (renewal Rs 750); all plus 18% GST
unit: Rs + GST, corporate (Pvt Ltd) ARN registration
source_title: AMFI, 'ARN Registration and Renewal fees applicable from 01-Oct-2024'
notes: ARN valid 3 years (Cafemutual / Wealthy). Each person selling/advising needs NISM Series V-A and an EUIN. Time: ARN typically issued in days-weeks after NISM pass (advisory sources; not verified from AMFI).

claim: NISM Series V-A (Mutual Fund Distributors) exam fee Rs 1,500 + GST per attempt (~Rs 1,770 all-in)
source_title: Wealthy partner blog 'NISM Series V A Exam: Fees, Validity & Attempts Explained'; Gromo 2026 guide
notes: Distributor-platform sources, not NISM's own fee page. Certificate valid 3 years.

claim: Execution-Only Platform framework (from 1-Sep-2023): Category 1 EOP registers with AMFI as agent of AMCs, DIRECT plans only (no regular plans), min net worth Rs 1 crore, fee capped at Rs 2 per transaction (excl. payment gateway); Category 2 EOP registers as a stock broker on the exchanges' EOP segment as agent of investors
unit: Rs per transaction (Cat-1 EOP fee cap)
source_title: AMFI Guidelines for Category-1 EOPs; SEBI EOP framework (Aug-2023) as reported by India Briefing
notes: Business-model fork: as an ARN holder the app earns trail on REGULAR plans; as an EOP it earns only Rs 2/transaction on DIRECT plans. It cannot be both for the same investor-product. At Rs 10-100/day, Rs 2/txn is 2-20% of the amount and would likely be borne by AMCs only under the cap.

claim: A distributor earns trail only on regular plans; for liquid funds the regular-direct TER gap (proxy for trail) is small, e.g. HDFC Liquid Fund 0.25% regular vs 0.17% direct = 8 bps
source_title: Value Research Online fund pages, HDFC Liquid Fund Regular / Direct (via search summary)
notes: Range for model: low 5 bps, base 8 bps, high 15 bps p.a. on liquid AUM; overnight funds near 0. Wealthy/Belong guides put liquid gap at 0.05-0.20% (secondary). On Rs 10,000 of liquid AUM, 8 bps = Rs 8/year per worker. The TER date on the VRO page was not confirmed.

claim: SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, 2026 replaced the 1996 Regulations from 1-Apr-2026: TER split into a Base Expense Ratio (incl. distributor payouts) plus statutory levies charged at actuals; AMFI circular 123/2025-26 (12-Mar-2026) changed how commissions accrue/pay
source_title: Mondaq, 'SEBI's 2026 Mutual Fund Regulations Overhaul: Lower TERs...'; Value Research 'SEBI Mutual Fund Regulations 2026'
notes: Secondary sources; SEBI gazette text not opened. Direction is lower TER caps, i.e. downward pressure on trail. Board approval reported 17-Dec-2025.

claim: Instant Access Facility in liquid (and overnight) funds: up to the lower of Rs 50,000 or 90% of the latest value of the investment, per day per scheme per investor; resident investors, online only; optional for AMCs
unit: Rs per day per scheme (or 90%, lower)
population: Resident investors in liquid/overnight schemes offering IAF
source_title: SEBI Master Circular for Mutual Funds (27-Jun-2024) - IAF limit (as reproduced by PPFAS MF IAF page)
notes: Covers emergency withdrawal for a worker; above that, normal redemption. AMC-optional, so pick AMCs that offer it.

claim: Regulatory maximum for paying MF redemption proceeds is 3 working days (T+3); liquid funds settle T+1 in practice
population: All MF schemes (5 days for >=80% overseas schemes)
source_title: SEBI circular SEBI/HO/IMD/IMD-I DOF2/P/CIR/2022/161 'Timelines for transfer of dividend and redemption proceeds to unitholders'
notes: CORRECTION of framing: T+1 for liquid funds is market practice/AMC scheme terms, not a SEBI mandate; SEBI's hard limit is T+3 (15% p.a. interest for delay). I did not find a primary source stating a T+1 mandate for liquid funds.

claim: Daily SIPs exist but minimums are typically Rs 100: Axis MF daily/weekly/monthly SIP min Rs 100 (multiples of Re 1, min 6 instalments); LIC MF cut daily SIP to Rs 100 incl. LIC MF Liquid Fund from 16-Oct-2024; ICICI Pru, Tata, HDFC, UTI also offer daily SIP
source_title: Axis MF knowledge centre 'Guide to starting mutual fund SIPs with Rs 100'; BusinessToday 'LIC Mutual Fund reduces daily SIP amount to Rs 100' (15-Oct-2024)
notes: KEY CONSTRAINT: Rs 10-99/day saves are below most daily-SIP minimums, so the app must either accumulate in the investor's bank/UPI balance and invest in Rs 100+ lots, or use AMCs allowing smaller lumpsums (Axis page says the smallest MF investment 'is 10 rupees' - lumpsum; unverified per scheme). The app may not pool worker money itself (see BUDS row).

claim: Since Apr-2024 KRAs classify KYC as Validated / Registered / On-Hold; only Aadhaar-validated ('KYC Validated') records can invest with a new AMC without re-KYC; 73% of 108.3 mn records were validated at 31-Mar-2024
source_title: Business Standard, 'Over 73% of KYC records validated, systems in place for remaining: KRAs' (24-Apr-2024)
notes: First-time gig investors will need fresh Aadhaar-based KYC (see e-KYC cost rows).

claim: KRA charges to intermediaries: Rs 30 per KYC upload, Rs 35 per download, modification nil (plus taxes) - NDML KRA schedule
unit: Rs per KYC upload (+ Rs 35 per download)
source_title: NDML KRA Circular NDML/POLICY/2012-0003 'Charge Structure'
notes: Primary document but dated 2012; I could not confirm current (2026) KRA tariffs. Use as a floor: base Rs 35, low Rs 30, high Rs 50 per new investor (high is an assumption).

claim: NPCI OC-223 (7-Oct-2025) 'Enhancement of UPI Autopay': users can VIEW all active Autopay mandates in any UPI app and PORT mandates between apps (in addition to existing revoke/pause/modify); live by 31-Dec-2025
population: All UPI members (payer PSPs, payee PSPs, apps)
source_title: NPCI circular NPCI/UPI/OC-223/2025-26 'Enhancement of UPI Autopay' (signed Sourabh Tomar, Head UPI Product)
notes: Read from the circular image. Brief says 'view/cancel from any UPI app' - the circular's new rights are VIEW and PORT (revoke/pause/modify already existed in the app holding the mandate). Other rules: porting is user-driven only, NO inducements (cashback, nudges, banners) to solicit porting; port only once per rolling 90 days; payer apps may not use 'view mandate' data for other purposes; payee PSP must issue a unique Merchant Identifier Code (MIC) mandatory for purpose code 'AZ'; merchants may execute via any UPI ID with the MIC. Implication: a competitor app can show and pull away the worker's savings mandate, and the app cannot bribe to retain.

claim: Autopay mandate execution must be initiated only in non-peak hours (before 10:00, 13:00-17:00, after 21:30), with max one execution attempt plus up to three retries
source_title: NPCI circular NPCI/UPI/OC/215/2025-26 'Guidelines on usage of UPI API' (21-May-2025), as summarised by Mondaq 'NPCI Guidelines On UPI And API Usage'
notes: Compliance by 31-Jul-2025/1-Aug-2025. Circular number from TeamLease/complinity summaries; primary PDF not opened. Republic World (5-May-2026) reports morning EMIs/SIPs declining in 2026 where banks scheduled executions in the 10:00-13:00 window or failed to send the 24h pre-debit notice - no NPCI failure statistics given (unverified). Schedule daily debits for early morning (e.g., 06:00-09:30) after the pre-debit notice.

claim: UPI Autopay supports DAILY frequency mandates (options: one-time, daily, weekly, fortnightly, monthly, bi-monthly, quarterly, half-yearly, yearly, as-presented)
source_title: Paytm blog 'Daily, Weekly, Monthly: Exploring All UPI AutoPay Frequency'; Tribune (NPCI launch of UPI Autopay, 2020)
notes: Not confirmed from an NPCI primary document (NPCI's BHIM page mentions 'monthly, quarterly etc'). Tribune quoting NPCI at launch lists daily. Each daily debit still needs a 24h pre-debit notice, so a daily mandate = ~2 messages/day/user (pre + post).

claim: RBI Digital Payments - E-mandate Framework, 2026 (21-Apr-2026) consolidates 2019-2024 circulars: recurring debits up to Rs 15,000 without additional factor of authentication; up to Rs 1,00,000 for MF subscriptions, insurance premiums and credit-card bill payments; first transaction needs AFA; pre-debit notification at least 24h before each debit (merchant, amount, date/time, mandate ref, reason); customer can opt out of any debit or withdraw the mandate; NO charge to customers for e-mandate facility
unit: Rs per debit without AFA (Rs 1,00,000 for MF/insurance/card bills)
source_title: LexOrbis, 'RBI's Digital Payments E-Mandate Framework, 2026' (circular RBI/CO.DPSS.POLC.No.S56/02.14.003/2026-27); RBI circular 12-Dec-2023 (Rs 1 lakh categories)

source_title: Vinod Kothari Consultants, 'RBI Proposes Regulation of NBFC Interest Rates and Pricing Methodology' (Aug-2026)
notes: Draft; consultant summary only. If finalised, compresses APR on exactly the Rs 5k-50k loans a gig-worker app would source - and therefore the lender's room to pay LSP fees.

claim: Prize Chits and Money Circulation Schemes (Banning) Act 1978 s.3 bans promoting/conducting, enrolling in, or receiving/remitting money for any prize chit or money circulation scheme; a 'prize chit' (s.2(e)) is collecting money by subscriptions/contributions for a scheme distributing prizes or gifts by lot or draw (or refunding with bonus), conventional chits excluded; penalty up to 3 years (minimum 1 year absent special reasons) and fine
population: Anyone promoting or joining such schemes
source_title: Prize Chits and Money Circulation Schemes (Banning) Act, 1978 ss.2(c), 2(e), 3, 4 (Indian Kanoon)
notes: Exempt (s.11): schemes by State Governments, state-owned companies, banking institutions, notified charitable/educational bodies. SC in RBI v Peerless General Finance (1987) read the two limbs conjunctively - collection of money AND prize by lot/draw. A 'save Rs 50/day and enter a weekly lucky draw' mechanic run by a non-bank app is squarely at risk. Prize-linked savings would need a bank/State scheme to run it (legal opinion needed).

claim: Chit Funds Act 1982: a 'chit' is an agreement where a specified number of persons subscribe periodic instalments and each in turn takes the prize amount by lot/auction/tender; no chit may be commenced or conducted without prior State Government sanction and registration (s.4); contravention punishable with up to 2 years and/or fine up to Rs 5,000
source_title: The Chit Funds Act, 1982 ss.2(b), 4, 76 (India Code; Indian Kanoon)
notes: Any 'savings circle' feature where members pool and one member takes the pot each period is a chit and needs state registration per state. Keep all savings individual and in the worker's own MF folio/FD.

claim: Banning of Unregulated Deposit Schemes Act 2019: 'deposit' = money received by advance, loan or any other form with a promise to return (with or without interest/bonus); accepting unregulated deposits punishable with 2-7 years and Rs 3-10 lakh fine; default on repayment 3-10 years; repeat offenders 5-10 years and up to Rs 5 crore
population: Any deposit taker other than regulated schemes
source_title: Banning of Unregulated Deposit Schemes Act, 2019 s.2(4) and penalty sections (India Code; PRS summary)
notes: The app must never hold worker money even transiently: collection must go from the worker's account straight to the AMC (via RBI-authorised PA) or the bank FD. Also MF rules require payment from the investor's own account (REG-066). Any 'wallet balance' held by the app = deposit risk + PA/PPI licensing issue.

claim: MF distributors may not rebate or pass back commission to investors and must not attract investors through rebates, gifts or gift vouchers (SEBI-mandated AMFI Code of Conduct for intermediaries)
source_title: AMFI Code of Conduct for MF Distributors (as published by HDFC MF / Canara Robeco MF distributor pages); SEBI circular on Code of Conduct for intermediaries
notes: Rules out 'cashback on your SIP' or referral bonuses paid to investors out of MF commission. A non-MF-linked engagement reward funded by other revenue is a grey area - get a legal opinion; EOP route (REG-038) has its own AMFI conduct rules. Choti SIP bars transaction charges to investors.

claim: Insurance Act 1938 s.41 (as amended 2015): no person may offer any rebate of commission or premium as an inducement to take out, renew or continue insurance; penalty up to Rs 10 lakh
source_title: Insurance Act, 1938 s.41 (Indian Kanoon)
notes: Only rebates allowed in the insurer's published prospectus/tables are permitted. The Sep-2026 IRDAI draft adds clawbacks and seller-level public mis-selling records.

claim: DPDP Rules 2025 notified 13-Nov-2025 with phased commencement: Data Protection Board provisions immediately; Consent Manager registration (Rule 4) from 13-Nov-2026; substantive fiduciary obligations, data-principal rights and penalties (Act ss.3-5, 6(1)-(8),(10), 7-17, 28-34; Rules 3, 5-16, 22, 23) from 13-May-2027
population: All data fiduciaries processing digital personal data in India
source_title: Commencement notification G.S.R. 843(E) of 13-Nov-2025 as summarised by dpdprules.org / ConsentOS / S&R Associates
notes: Several law-firm and tracker sources agree on the three dates; MeitY gazette PDF not opened (403). No evidence found of the 18-month window being shortened.

claim: DPDP Act 2023: processing needs consent (or a listed legitimate use); consent must be free, specific, informed, unconditional, unambiguous and limited to the specified purpose (s.6(1)); data collected before commencement may be processed only after a fresh notice and stops on withdrawal (s.5(2)); max penalties Rs 250 cr (security safeguards), Rs 200 cr (breach notification / children), Rs 50 cr (other)
unit: Rs crore max penalty per breach (security safeguards)
source_title: DPDP Act 2023 ss.5-6 and Schedule (dpdpact2023.com; FPF explainer; DPDP penalty trackers)
notes: Penalty provisions bite only from 13-May-2027. Until then IT Act s.43A + SPDI Rules 2011 apply (financial information is 'sensitive personal data' - consent and purpose limits), and IT Act s.72A criminalises disclosure of personal information obtained under a lawful contract without consent (up to 3 years / Rs 5 lakh).

claim: Using Bueno's borrower list for the new product is NOT permissible on the founder's own authority: the data belongs to Bueno's successor (BetterPlace acquired Bueno on 8-May-2023), was collected for lending on behalf of partner lenders, and a new savings/cross-sell purpose is not the 'specified purpose'
source_title: Analysis from DPDP s.6(1)/s.5(2), IT Act s.43A/SPDI Rules and s.72A, RBI DL Directions 2025 para 13; acquisition date from EdTechReview/Tracxn
notes: Legal analysis, not a court ruling - get counsel. Layers: (1) no right - fiduciary is BetterPlace/the lenders, not the founder; (2) purpose limitation - borrowers consented to credit processing, not marketing of a new app; (3) as an LSP Bueno could store only minimal data for the RE-LSP agreement (DL para 13); (4) credit data from bureaus is further restricted under CICRA (not researched). Lawful route: BetterPlace (as fiduciary) sends a consented opt-in invite, or acquire users fresh. Marketing SMS/calls also need TRAI TCCCPR/DLT compliance (not researched).

claim: Credit-card sourcing: the decision to issue stays with the card-issuer; DSAs/DMAs/other agents may only solicit/service, and the issuer is liable for their acts; co-branding partners are limited to marketing/distribution and may not access card transaction data; unsolicited cards prohibited, written/explicit consent required; NBFCs need prior RBI approval (and Rs 100 cr NOF) to issue cards
source_title: RBI Master Direction - Credit Card and Debit Card - Issuance and Conduct Directions, 2022
notes: The MD has no specific provisions on FD-secured cards. Combine with: no DLG on credit cards (REG-007); a bank cannot lend against another bank's FD (REG-029) - so the FD must sit at the card-issuing bank. Sourcing fee per card is commercial (not researched/unverified).

claim: Insurance Marketing Firm (IRDAI IMF Regulations 2015): application fee Rs 5,000; principal officer must pass IMF exam; may tie up with max 2 life, 2 general, 2 health insurers; may also distribute other financial products permitted by RBI/SEBI/PFRDA/DoP with their approvals; net worth per regulations (amount not shown on IRDAI page)
